description:
## Why

`pkix-lint::Deviation` and `DeviationStore` carry the project's bespoke 'this rule does not apply here' override mechanism. OSCAL has the same concept built in: a Risk with `status=deviation-approved` referencing the affected Finding(s), with remediation guidance and approval audit trail.

## What

Replace the `Deviation` and `DeviationStore` types with OSCAL Risk objects:

**OSCAL Risk fields:**
- `uuid` — generated.
- `title`, `description` — what the deviation is.
- `statement` — the rationale text.
- `status` — `open`, `investigating`, `remediating`, `deviation-requested`, `deviation-approved`, `closed`. For our case typically `deviation-approved` or `deviation-requested`.
- `origins[]` — who approved (audit trail).
- `threat-ids[]` — optional reference to standardised threat catalogs.
- `characterizations[]` — facets of the risk.
- `mitigating-factors[]` — why the deviation is acceptable.
- `remediations[]` — planned actions if any.
- `related-observations[]` — pointers to the Observations the deviation covers (i.e., the cert/chain/SAN-entry scope).
- `subjects[]` — scope (issuer DN, subject DN, serial range, policy OID, etc.) lands here as OSCAL Subjects with appropriate `subject-uuid` / `type` fields.

**Scope axes** (previously PKIX-8mzp's enum-variant proposals):
- IssuerDnExact → OSCAL Subject with `type=identified-subject`, prop carrying issuer DN.
- IssuerDnContains → same with `prop[name=dn-pattern]`.
- SerialRange → `prop[name=serial-range]`.
- SubjectDnContains, PolicyOid (PKIX-8mzp targets) → same pattern; new prop names.

The bespoke `DeviationScope` enum is retired. Subject-scoping is OSCAL-native: a Risk carries a `subjects` list with structured prop bags rather than a closed enum of scope kinds.

**Persistence** (previously PKIX-dbhe's scope):
- A 'Risk store' serializes as JSON arrays of OSCAL Risks.
- File-backed persistence is OSCAL Risks in a file (potentially alongside an Assessment Plan or POA&M for full OSCAL context).

## Acceptance

- [ ] No `Deviation` or `DeviatedFinding` types remain; replaced by Risk-shaped types.
- [ ] DeviationStore replaced by a Risk store with OSCAL-shaped persistence.
- [ ] Scope axes (issuer DN, serial range, etc.) all expressible via Risk `subjects` + `props`.
- [ ] PKIX-8mzp (DeviationScope::SubjectDnContains / PolicyOid) absorbed: the scope axes ARE expressible without growing a Rust enum.
- [ ] PKIX-dbhe (persistence) absorbed: Risk store serialization IS persistence.
- [ ] Serde round-trips against NIST OSCAL JSON Schema.

## Reshape impact

- PKIX-8mzp WONTFIX (closed with reason 'absorbed into PKIX-9vnx.5 — scope axes are OSCAL Subject props, not Rust enum variants').
- PKIX-dbhe WONTFIX (closed with reason 'absorbed into PKIX-9vnx.5 — Risk store IS the persistence layer').

## Depends on

PKIX-9vnx.2 (binding), PKIX-9vnx.4 (Risks reference Observations, so Observations must exist first).
notes:
Reframed 2026-05-11 (Arch 2 — see PKIX-ztmr / PKIX-9vnx notes):

- Title intent shifts from 'replace Deviation/DeviationStore WITH OSCAL Risk' to 'add OSCAL Risk serializer for Deviation; serialize DeviationStore as a JSON array of OSCAL Risks.'
- `pkix_lint::Deviation` Rust struct STAYS as pkix-lint's internal representation. It does NOT become an OSCAL Risk struct.
- Scope axes still don't grow Rust enum variants (per stance). Internal representation: open-ended `HashMap<String, String>` or `Vec<ScopeProp>` props bag — flexible enough that PKIX-8mzp's SubjectDnContains / PolicyOid land as new map keys, not new enum variants. Serializer emits them as OSCAL Subject props on the output Risk.
- DeviationStore persistence: serialize/deserialize as a JSON array of OSCAL Risk objects. Internally still a `Vec<Deviation>` or similar.
- No longer blocked by PKIX-9vnx.2 (closed). PKIX-8mzp and PKIX-dbhe stay reshaped under this; their notes already point here.
title: Realign Deviation/DeviationStore to OSCAL Risk + Risk store
